tone.notes: Words and voice are unchanged from the approved script: opens on the fact with no warm-up, asks "Okay, but why write it down?" and answers it, ends on the catchphrase. No call to action. It says the word "bug" is older than the moth instead of claiming the moth invented it.

banned_topics.notes: A piece of computing history. No politics, war, crime, advice, gore or copyable stunts. The popular myth is corrected on screen, not repeated. Edison and Harvard are named as historical facts, not used as characters. The new cut-out pictures (moth, computer cabinet, open book) are generic drawings, not a likeness of a real object or person.

visuals.notes: Re-rendered in render-paper-collage with continuous motion added at the person's request ("make it not just still"): torn sheets drift, loose scraps float up the page, strips hop in turn, notes sway and reveal their words one by one, tags swing, and each cutout hovers over a turning starburst (the moth flaps, the computer's reels turn and lights chase, the book turns a page). Reviewed the 8 sampled frames plus sheets of 2, 3 and 6 frames per second. All text readable and inside the safe area (11/11 automated checks); the quote note is present in every sampled frame. One fix during review: a drifting scrap passed behind Blink's head, so scraps now keep out of Blink's column. Known blemishes, not hiding any text: for about a third of a second at each beat change the page is bare while the new sheets slide in; beats with a single note leave the middle of the frame empty. Motion was judged from sampled frames, not watched at speed.

character.notes: Blink is on-model: mint-green egg blob, dark outline, round glasses, pink cheeks, sparkles. Full size on the hook, lower-left corner afterwards, expressions change per beat, nothing overlaps it now (the cut-out sits to its right). Blink is still drawn flat, not as a paper cut-out, so it sits slightly apart from the collage. The audio was not listened to; it is the same voice file as the previous render.

learnings: The person found the first collage render too still. Everything on screen should keep moving after it lands (drift, sway, hop, a looping action on each cutout); a piece that only slides in and stops reads as a slide show.
Keep drifting background scraps out of Blink's column, or one ends up sitting on Blink's head.
